comments.text:
Go through tiny house plans- and consider putting your tiny house on a basement foundation! You can DOUBLE or TRIPLE your space for $25-$50K Concrete pour! You can pour a FULL basement- kitchenette, living room, bathroom, bedroom, with a basement! It depends where you live, but anywhere a basement is possible, it’s a huge win of extra space for far less money! My goal is to buy a cheap, rural, piece of land, and build a tiny house. I plan to build a full basement foundation, and a 750 square foot “tiny house” new build. Yes, it’s bigger than a traditional “tiny house”, but it allows for most codes that require at least 700 square feet for a permit. So, in a very rural area In Pennsylvania, I’ve priced the following:
2 acres - $16K
A 1400 Sq Ft basement/garage foundation- $40K
Plans, for my builder- $10K
Custom, on site build , 750 sq ft 1 and a half story home- $50K
= $116K total build cost
Septic, Solar, Well, and Starlink- approximately $50K
Total cost adding in potential issues - $175 K
Now, you have a 2 car garage, a full basement level of either living space or an in law/college student apartment with a full bathroom, small kitchen, living area and bedroom! 1st floor master, full bathroom, kitchen, dining area, living room. 2nd story is loft type with bathroom, guest room on one side, office/tv space on the other! Now you literally own a 3 bedroom, 3 bathroom house, with garage, wrap around 2 level porch (the plans I bought included) and the only utility is your monthly Starlink subscription!

I lease a lot space in a quaint 12 unit community that is a natural reserve with a lake, wildlife, chickens, a huge fire pit, catch and release fishing docks, and a huge barn-dominium that serves as a community center.  No one needs to over spend on a TH or buy raw land that costs $$$$$ to install utilities.  Worrying about the value is not a concern to me as I purchased a home and not an investment, and the "fear" of the lease going up is no concern, either.  This type of lifestyle is not for everyone, but it works for me as a single, retired woman with zero debt, a fluffy savings account and the deep desire to live peacefully and thoughtfully the remainder of my days. A tiny home typically:
